about: Every claim the article makes that this POC is supposed to support, with where the evidence for it is. experiments/claims.py checks each entry against the run it names and writes docs/claim-evidence-matrix.md. Claims about the wider world (specifications, other people's writing) are not here: they are tracked in the article's research notes and checked as links.

fields.id: stable id, cited by the matrix
fields.section: the article section that makes the claim
fields.claim: what is asserted, in one sentence
fields.kind: measured (a number or outcome from the run), guaranteed (an invariant a test pins down), or scoped (a limit on what the evidence shows)
fields.facts: paths in runs/<id>/facts.json that carry the claim
fields.placeholders: article placeholders that print those values (runs/<id>/article-evidence.json)
fields.verified_by: checks in runs/<id>/verification.json that recompute them from the raw records
fields.evidence: files inside the run directory, as globs
fields.tests: tests that pin the behaviour down, as file::test
fields.limits: what the evidence does not show

claims.claim: The platform ran INC-4917 end to end with gpt-oss:20b: a median 44 s to the approval request and 5 s after it.
claims.limits: one scenario on one machine; the approval wait is excluded by construction, not measured

claims.claim: A run cost a median of 24,002 tokens across 12 model calls.
claims.limits: token counts are what Ollama reported for these prompts; another prompt or model changes them

claims.claim: All eight checks passed in every one of the three runs, for both models.
claims.limits: three runs per model on one scenario: regression evidence, not a reliability estimate

claims.claim: The rollback reached the backend exactly once in every completed run.
claims.limits: the backend is the POC's mock system of record, which enforces the key; a real system has to do the same

claims.section: Tools Belong Behind an Action Boundary
claims.claim: A production write runs only under the digest a human approved, re-verified at the gateway.
claims.limits: approvals are simulated: a request records who decided, not a real identity provider

claims.section: Tools Belong Behind an Action Boundary
claims.claim: A denied action never reached a backend; policy rejects a direct Kubernetes rollback of a GitOps service before any approval is asked for.
claims.limits: the monolith's zero direct rollbacks are what the model chose in three runs, not a control it enforces

claims.claim: The diagnosis agent's context was 550 estimated tokens from 4 cited sources.
claims.limits: an estimate from the assembler's own token counts, not the model's tokenizer

claims.claim: The diagnosis agent read evidence 8 times in the run the article walks through, and 7 to 8 times across all runs.
claims.limits: how many reads a model makes is its own behaviour, not a platform guarantee

claims.claim: An expired memory is never recalled, and a memory without a source is rejected.
claims.limits: the memories are seeded for this incident; the article states no number from them

claims.claim: One workflow survived two SIGKILLs across three processes, and the backend recorded one rollback.
claims.limits: a kill is not every failure mode; the machine, the disk and SQLite all survived

claims.claim: The investigation cost 18,231 tokens before the first crash and 912 after it, so nothing was investigated twice.
claims.limits: one crash sequence in one run

claims.section: "The Agent Failed" Is Not an Operational Signal
claims.claim: A resumed process joins the trace the killed process started, so one incident stays one trace.
claims.limits: spans are written to files by the POC's exporter; no collector or backend is involved

claims.claim: A lost write response produced 1 execution and 1 replay in the platform; the monolith, given the same fault, rolled back 2 times.
claims.limits: the fault is injected by the POC at a chosen point, not observed in the wild

claims.claim: Two injected timeouts on a read were retried with backoff and succeeded on attempt 3, without changing workflow state.
claims.limits: one read tool, one retry budget

claims.claim: Three requirement changes, written as patches for both designs, touched the files and lines the article lists, and the layered tree still passed its import contracts after each one.
claims.limits: three changes written by one author, illustrative and not a benchmark

claims.claim: The monolith baseline took a median of 25 s and 14,614 tokens, and after a kill it asked for the same approval again 13 s later.
claims.limits: the baseline is a deliberately simple script, so it is a contrast, not a competitor

claims.claim: 33 tests passed with the cited run, 29 without a model and 4 against the local models, and the 7 import contracts hold.
claims.limits: the counts are from this run's sittings; they change as tests are added

claims.claim: The remediation agent's first structured answer failed its contract in 4 of 6 runs, and the one bounded repair fixed it each time.
claims.limits: a property of these prompts and these two models, not of structured output in general

claims.claim: Swapping gpt-oss:20b for qwen3:8b was a configuration change, and the platform ran unchanged.
claims.limits: both models are local Ollama models behind one adapter; a hosted provider adds its own concerns

claims.claim: A reader can reproduce the article's numbers without a model server, because the run the article cites was recorded and can be replayed.
claims.limits: a replay reproduces the recorded model traffic, so it proves the pipeline and the counts, not that a live model answers the same way again

claims.claim: The six layers are this article's synthesis, not a standard, and the POC is one way to draw them.
claims.limits: no standards body defines these layers; the import contracts only show that this drawing holds in this code

claims.claim: MCP, Ollama, SQLite durability, process kills and OpenTelemetry spans are real; the enterprise systems, chat payloads, approvals, faults and identities are simulated.
claims.limits: every number in the article comes from this simulated world, so it shows the platform's behaviour, not production performance

claims.claim: The POC does not measure model quality and runs one scenario three times per model.
claims.limits: no held-out set, no second incident, no statistical claim
